title: Bidirectional Dijkstra in Lisbon’s Alfama!
description: Watch Bidirectional Dijkstra race across Alfama’s winding street graph from start to destination. The search expands from both ends and meets in the middle to reduce explored paths dramatically.
ig_caption:
🗺️✨ Alfama’s streets aren’t just beautiful—they’re a weighted graph! In this reel, **Bidirectional Dijkstra** runs **two synchronized Dijkstra searches**: one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal node, using edge weights (e.g., distance/time) to guarantee optimality. 🤝

📌 **Deep technical idea:** Instead of expanding outward from just one side, we maintain two priority queues and stop when the forward+backward frontier has found a best meeting cost (based on the current min distances and an upper bound). This typically cuts the search space on large real-world graphs, especially when the start and goal are far apart. 

🔎 **Graph theory on real street maps:** Each intersection becomes a vertex, each road segment becomes a weighted edge, and the algorithm finds the shortest path in the graph metric—perfect for mapping, routing, and navigation demos.

fb_caption:

By running graph search from both the start and the destination simultaneously, the algorithm meets in the middle—often exploring far fewer nodes while still guaranteeing an optimal path.
